subject: c12-phy

weightage.label: Unit II–IV — Current Electricity; Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism; Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
Unit VII–VIII — Dual Nature; Atoms and Nuclei

note: Official CBSE theory paper: 70 marks. The syllabus gives marks by unit groups, not individual chapter weightage. Practical is separate: 30 marks. NCERT content explicitly excluded for 2026-27 is not assessed.
mistakes: Mixing scalar and vector quantities or dropping vector direction/signs in field, force and magnetic-effect problems.
Using the wrong geometry or distance variable in Coulomb, Gauss-law, potential and capacitance problems.
Confusing emf, terminal voltage, resistance, resistivity and conductivity in current-electricity questions.
Applying Kirchhoff's rules without first choosing consistent loop/current directions and then carrying the signs consistently.
Using right-hand-rule directions mechanically without checking the actual vector cross-product direction.
Confusing magnetic field due to a current element, force on a moving charge, and force on a current-carrying conductor.
In AC problems, mixing peak and RMS quantities or using reactance/impedance formulas with inconsistent units.
In optics, mixing sign conventions between mirror, lens and refraction problems.
In wave optics, confusing path difference, phase difference, fringe width and fringe position.
In modern physics, confusing work function, threshold frequency, stopping potential, binding energy and mass defect.
In semiconductor questions, drawing p-n junction/rectifier characteristics without labelling the relevant regions and terminals.
order: Start with Electrostatics and Current Electricity; build a clean base of field, potential, capacitance, current and circuit reasoning.
Do Moving Charges and Magnetism before Magnetism and Matter, then connect both to electromagnetic induction.
Study AC immediately after EMI so phasors, reactance, impedance, resonance and transformer ideas stay connected.
Complete Optics as one block: Ray Optics first, then Wave Optics.
Finish Dual Nature, Atoms and Nuclei together because they form the modern-physics sequence.
Finish Semiconductor Electronics with diagrams and characteristic curves, then solve mixed numericals and conceptual questions.
Use timed mixed practice across units rather than practising only one chapter type repeatedly.
